answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A dawn delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A voyage check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A summit penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 10305 identities need 10305 bonds of 28 tokens, 16247 dollars of hardware and 35 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
